lines.text: I had beaten the Stone. For about as long as it takes to breathe in.
Majesty, the Order accepts the Stone's verdict. Lucan Varr is a zero. Twice measured, twice nothing.
And the Charter is very plain. A lord's privileges belong to a lord. A man who lights nothing before his King is no lord at all.
And there it was. The trap behind the trap.

No privileges meant no Fourth Article. Nothing to stop the Order measuring me again, somewhere quiet, for as long as it liked. And my name on the Northern Compact was worth exactly what I'd just measured.
If I lit up, I was hollow-born. If I lit nothing, I was nobody. He had planned for both.
The Order will take the young man into its care. For his own protection.
Four Hounds in iron masks stepped out from the wall. Behind them stood Brother Caddoc, smiling. I couldn't prove he had ever left the city, and he knew it.
Uncle, he's a Varr. Hand a Varr to the Order, and every house in the midlands will remember it.
Make him your ward. The Eleventh Article. A ward of the Crown is the Crown's household. Nobody touches him without your seal. Not even the Order.
It was my own trick, the one I'd used for six children in Greyhollow. I had no idea anyone at court had read the Charter.
Yes. Yes, that. Lucan Varr is... a Royal Ward. In the Crown's keeping, until the Tourney ends. We will decide the rest then.
As Your Majesty pleases. Until the Tourney ends.
He didn't argue. That frightened me more than anything. He had me exactly where he wanted me: in Aldcrown, half a kingdom from every thread I had, and unable to leave.
Afterwards, in a corridor, Mirelle caught up with me.
Don't thank me. I read the Charter when I was nine. Nobody else in my family ever has.
I wasn't going to thank you. I was going to ask if Royal Wards get breakfast.
The Crown's keeping was a tower room in the old palace, with a guard on the door. The guard was Captain Holt.
My lord. My men would be bones in Kesting Pass but for you. If I have to guard you, I'll guard you properly. From everyone.
I had made six children my wards, to keep them from the Order. Now a king had done the same for me. I couldn't decide if that was funny.
Without my name, the Compact was three lords and a tribe. Exactly the sort of thing a king sends an army against. I thought of Bram, building his wall in the snow, and hoped it was a good one.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty, coming soon.
